cdl-entry-level-driver-training-eldt-tan.title: CDL Entry Level Driver Training (ELDT) Tanker (N) Endorsement

modules.title: Lesson 1: Regulatory Overview
desc: Introduces the federal regulations and safety standards that govern tank vehicle operations. Students will gain an understanding of applicable FMCSA requirements, CDL tank endorsement rules, and the driver’s legal responsibilities before operating a tank vehicle. Emphasis is placed on compliance, permit, and endorsement requirements, route considerations, and the importance of understanding how regulations are designed to reduce risk associated with liquid cargo movement.

modules.title: Lesson 2: Tank Vehicles Operation and Inspection
desc: Focuses on the safe operation and inspection of tank vehicles. Students will learn how tank design features such as bulkheads, baffles, and smooth-bore tanks affect vehicle handling and liquid surge. The lesson covers proper pre-trip inspection procedures, including checking valves, manhole covers, hoses, and emergency shutoff systems. Operational topics include safe driving techniques, surge control, curve and ramp management, and the effects of partial loads.

modules.title: Final Examination
desc: Test your knowledge and ensure you are prepared to operate tank vehicles safely and in compliance with federal regulations.

faqs: I already have my learner’s permit in hand. Do I need to take more tests in this course, or is it just a precursor to take the test I have already passed?
If you already have your CDL learner’s permit in hand, then you have already passed the written permit tests required by your state.

This ELDT course is not another DMV permit test. It is the federally required Entry-Level Driver Training (ELDT) theory training that must be completed and submitted to the FMCSA Training Provider Registry before you can take your CDL behind-the-wheel skills test (pre-trip, backing, and road test).
You will complete quizzes and a final exam within the course itself, but those are for training completion purposes only and are separate from the DMV permit exams you already passed.

entry-level-driver-training-eldt-hazmat-.title: CDL Entry Level Driver Training (ELDT) - Hazmat and Tank Vehicle (X) Endorsement

modules.title: Module 1: Hazmat Basic Requirements and Communication
desc: Foundational hazardous materials competencies and the DOT Hazardous Materials Regulations (HMR) and FMCSR requirements that apply to drivers: the hazardous materials table, marking, labeling and placarding, shipping papers, and the reporting channels to use during a hazmat emergency.
lessons: Lesson 1: Basic Introductory Hazardous Materials Requirements
Lesson 3: Reporting Hazardous Materials Crashes and Releases

modules.title: Module 2: Safe Transportation Practices
desc: Practical procedures for moving hazardous materials safely: tunnel and railroad-crossing rules, loading and unloading, segregation and securement, hazmat near foodstuffs, and bulk packages including cargo tanks and portable tanks.
lessons: Lesson 4: Tunnels and Railroad (RR)-Highway Grade Crossing Requirements
Lesson 5: Loading and Unloading Hazardous Materials
Lesson 6: Hazardous Materials on Passenger Vehicles
Lesson 8: Tank Vehicles Operation and Inspection

modules.title: Module 3: Emergency Preparedness and Response
desc: How to respond to crashes and unintended releases, including reporting procedures and emergency-response practices that protect people, property, and the environment.

modules.title: Module 4: Pre-Trip and Operational Considerations
desc: Pre-trip tire checks and the FMCSA rules on fueling while transporting hazardous materials.

modules.title: Module 5: Planning and Permits
desc: Route planning, selecting compliant routes, when a Hazardous Materials Safety Permit (HMSP) is required, and operating under an HMSP.

modules.title: Final Examination
desc: A final theory assessment covering hazmat and tank-vehicle content.

lessons: Lesson 1: Basic Introductory Hazardous Materials Requirements
Lesson 3: Reporting Hazardous Materials Crashes and Releases

modules.title: Practice Examination
desc: Test your knowledge and ensure you're ready to handle hazardous materials safely and in compliance with regulations.

Note: There is no separate training required for the X endorsement. Drivers obtain it by completing the H (HazMat) endorsement training and passing the DMV knowledge test for the N (Tanker) endorsement, which together authorize the transport of hazardous materials in tank vehicles.
